subject: general
question: Three taps A, B and C together can fill an empty cistern in 20 minutes. Tap A alone can fill it in 50 minutes and tap B alone in 60 minutes. How long will tap C alone take to fill it (in minutes)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency of **A + B + C** = 1/20

Efficiency of **A** = 1/50, Efficiency of **B** = 1/60

Efficiency of **C** = 1/20 − (1/50 + 1/60) = 3/60 − (1.2/60 + 1/60) = (15 − 6 − 5)/300 = 4/300 = 1/75

**∴ The correct answer is 75 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Person/Tap**

⇒ Efficiency of **A + B + C** = 15 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 6 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 5 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = (A + B + C) − A − B

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = 15 − 6 − 5 = 4 units/min

⇒ Time taken by **C** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by **C** = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 75 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in **x** hours and an outlet pipe empties it in **y** hours, the net part filled in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y).

Negative Efficiency

In pipe systems, an outlet pipe (drain pipe) is always assigned a **negative efficiency** because it removes work/water from the system.</p
